news.title: Democrats secure 56-seat Senate majority as Peltola wins Alaska
news.text:
Democrat Mary Peltola has defeated Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan to win Alaska’s United States Senate race, ending the last unresolved Senate contest in the 2026 midterm elections and expanding her party’s majority in the chamber to 56 seats.

Peltola’s victory, projected on Tuesday, November 17, gives Democrats a 56–44 majority in the Senate after the party flipped nine Republican-held seats in the midterm elections.

According to the Alaska Division of Elections’ preliminary results, Peltola secured 50.1 per cent of first-choice votes, crossing the threshold required to win outright under the state’s ranked-choice voting system without a further round of counting.

Sullivan received 45.8 per cent, while Daniel J. Sullivan, another candidate whose name became central to the controversy surrounding the election, received 1.7 per cent. Republican Gerald Heikes polled 2.1 per cent.

The Associated Press, in a report published by ABC News on Wednesday, November 18, said Peltola overcame allegations that members of her campaign helped recruit a candidate who shares the incumbent senator’s name.

The election was marked by allegations of political manipulation, competing investigations and legal battles over the possibility of voters confusing the two candidates named Sullivan.

Controversy over two Dan Sullivans

The controversy intensified following an October 28 investigation by The New York Times, which reported that operatives aligned with Peltola’s campaign, her lawyers and senior aides at the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee were involved in efforts to recruit Republican challengers to enter the race.

One of the candidates was Daniel J. Sullivan, a resident of Petersburg, Alaska, whose name closely resembles that of incumbent Senator Dan S. Sullivan.

The newspaper reported that the recruitment effort, internally referred to as a ballot-composition project, was intended to dilute support for the incumbent and improve Peltola’s chances of winning.

ABC News also reported that the Times based its investigation on interviews, text messages and documents.

However, Peltola’s campaign denied involvement in recruiting either Sullivan candidate.

The controversy prompted President Donald Trump to accuse Peltola of election fraud and call for her prosecution.

The Justice Department subsequently filed a lawsuit seeking to prevent certification of the election if the incumbent Sullivan lost by a margin smaller than the votes received by the similarly named candidate.

A federal judge dismissed the lawsuit, but the Justice Department appealed the decision.

Victory despite legal battles

Despite the controversy, Peltola secured a decisive enough lead to win without relying on additional ranked-choice calculations.

Alaska Public Media reported that her 50.1 per cent share of first-choice votes exceeded the combined votes received by the two Sullivans and Heikes.

The Justice Department’s investigation into the alleged recruitment effort remains ongoing, while the civil case continues through the appeals process.

Peltola’s victory makes her the first Democrat elected to the US Senate from Alaska since 2008 and the first Alaska Native person to serve in the chamber.

She previously represented Alaska in the House of Representatives, becoming the first Alaska Native woman elected to Congress in 2022.

Her campaign focused on affordability, healthcare costs, living expenses and the interests of Alaska residents.

The result also completes the Senate race count in the 2026 midterm elections, giving Democrats a substantial majority when the new Congress convenes in January.
news.summary:
Democrat Mary Peltola has defeated Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan to win Alaska’s United States Senate race, ending the last unresolved Senate contest in the 2026 midterm elections and expanding her party’s majority in the chamber to 56 seats.

news.title: Xi, Putin meet ahead of historic Trump trilateral summit
news.text:
Shenzhen, China: Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin began talks in Shenzhen on Wednesday, a day ahead of a historic three-way summit with Donald Trump in the southern Chinese city.

Thursday’s trilateral has triggered fears that the three powerful men could decide the fate of Ukraine over the heads of Kyiv and Europe, and seek to carve up the world into 21st-century spheres of influence.

Washington had signalled that Ukraine — something Xi vehemently sees as not China’s problem — was not expected to be addressed, before Trump said that it would.

China has said only that the leaders would hold “in-depth exchanges on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations” on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting.

Also up for discussion are the Iran war and nuclear disarmament, according to Washington, after a US-Russia bilateral treaty on atomic weapons expired in February.

Beijing has long maintained that the US and Russia should reduce their giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its smaller stockpile.

 In from the cold 

Chinese and Russian news agencies reported at around noon on Wednesday that Xi and Putin had met for talks — the fifth time the two leaders have met this year, including once by video link.

Putin has been shunned by the West since launching Europe’s worst conflict since World War II with his 2022 attack on Ukraine.

Addressing the APEC gathering on Wednesday, he said he expected the trilateral summit with Xi and Trump to be “highly useful.”

“At a time when military-political risks are on the rise, what is desperately needed is unity rather than division... and dialogue rather than ultimatums,” Putin said.

He said Western sanctions imposed on Russia since his 2022 invasion of Ukraine had failed, arguing that they were “not capable of fully stopping growth or destroying the economies of the competition.”

Earlier, Xi called for greater international cooperation on AI and free trade.

“Starting by lowering tariffs, expanding access and exploring regulations and management standards, China will conduct deep-seated reform,” Xi said as he opened the event.

Xi and Putin were expected to discuss energy and finance and then — in a smaller format — foreign policy including Ukraine and North Korea, Russian officials said.

Kim incoming? 

Trump was on Wednesday still in the Philippines where a day earlier he met fellow leaders of the Quad — Australia, Japan and India — for the first time in his second term.

The grouping is broadly aimed at counterbalancing China’s regional influence.

He said he was eyeing one-on-one talks with Putin and Kim Jong Un at his next stop in Shenzhen, saying the North Korean leader “would like” to meet in China.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Wednesday stopped short of confirming the meeting with Kim.

“If we have a problem with North Korea, the only way we’re ever going to solve it is if we engage with them,” Rubio said in Manila.

Trump was in the Philippines for a summit of the 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).

His visit saw protests by around 2,000 people carrying banners reading “Trump out now” and “Reject Pax Silica” — a reference to a US supply chain initiative.

 Tariffs, chips and rare earths 

While ASEAN leaders grappled with a raft of regional issues, the spectre of Trump’s ongoing tariff blitz has loomed large.

Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Monday slammed what he called a “countercurrent of unilateralism and protectionism” while touting Beijing’s own expanding trade with the bloc.

Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Canada’s Mark Carney sang a similar tune on trade, with both explicitly citing a need to wean themselves off dependence on the US market.

On Tuesday, a combative Trump showed no let-up in his trade war with Beijing, saying the United States would catch China in rare-earths production “within 10 months.”

Hours before Trump touched down in Manila, Washington announced new rules on the transfer of advanced AI chips, a move that could potentially rankle ASEAN members.

Companies shipping high-end chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia will now require a special license, as the countries were said to represent a “higher-than-normal risk of diversion.”

Singapore responded by saying it was now exploring ways to facilitate “trusted access” for firms based in the city-state.
news.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin met in Shenzhen ahead of a trilateral summit with US President Donald Trump. The meeting raises concerns about potential decisions regarding Ukraine and global spheres of influence.

news.title: Democrats Invoke Ted Cruz's Own Words in Bid to Block FCC Nominee Vote
news.text: Senate Democrats are urging Senator Ted Cruz to delay a committee vote on President Donald Trump's nominee to the Federal Communications Commission, citing the Texas Republican's own past opposition to confirming controversial nominees during a lame-duck session. All Democratic members of the Senate Commerce Committee, led by Ranking Member Maria Cantwell, asked Cruz to remove FCC nominee Danielle Thumann Severs from Wednesday's markup agenda and postpone consideration until the next Congress, when Democrats will control the Senate. They argued that any Republican FCC nominee should be considered alongside the renomination of Democratic Commissioner Anna Gomez and a Democratic nominee for another vacant commission seat. But Cruz appears intent on moving forward. "We look forward to reporting her out tomorrow and suggest Senate Democrats weigh in with the White House on nominating Democrats to the unfilled spot," committee spokesperson Blair Taylor told Politico. Newsweek has reached out to Cruz's office, the FCC and Thumann Severs for comment. Why It Matters The confirmation battle could help determine the partisan balance of the FCC, the independent agency that regulates telecommunications, broadcasting and broadband policy. If confirmed, Thumann Severs would join FCC Chairman Brendan Carr and Commissioner Olivia Trusty, giving Republicans a 3-1 advantage over the commission's lone Democrat, Anna Gomez. Critics have argued the move would allow Republicans to further advance Carr's agenda before Democrats take control of the Senate in January. The fight also comes as Democrats and outside advocacy groups raise questions about Thumann Severs' role in matters involving media regulation and broadcast licensing. What to Know In a letter dated November 16, Commerce Committee Democrats argued there was "no mandate for the outgoing majority to rush through a partisan FCC nomination in its final weeks" following elections that returned control of Congress to Democrats. They asked Cruz to remove the nomination from Wednesday's executive session and revisit it next year. The lawmakers pointedly quoted language Cruz used in 2014 regarding controversial nominees advanced after an election. "As you wrote in 2014, controversial nominees 'should not be confirmed in the lame duck session of Congress by senators who just lost their seats and are no longer accountable to the voters,'" the Democrats wrote. "We agree." Their letter argues that, because Democrats will control the Senate and the Commerce Committee next year, any FCC nomination should be handled through a bipartisan process that also includes the renomination of Gomez and the selection of a replacement for former Democratic Commissioner Geoffrey Starks. Who Is Danielle Thumann Severs? Thumann Severs currently serves as senior counsel to FCC Chairman Carr. She previously worked as a legal adviser in his office before taking a government affairs role at telecommunications infrastructure company Crown Castle and later returning to the FCC. Her portfolio has included issues related to broadband deployment, public safety, telecommunications infrastructure, and consumer affairs. Carr has praised her as an experienced communications policy attorney and public servant. The nomination would fill a Republican seat left vacant on the five-member commission. New Questions About Her Testimony The nomination fight has intensified following allegations from Senator Ben Ray Luján that internal FCC emails conflict with testimony Thumann Severs provided during her confirmation hearing earlier this month. According to Bloomberg, Luján said emails obtained through Freedom of Information Act requests indicate that Thumann Severs was involved in matters related to the Paramount-Skydance merger review, despite her testimony that she had not worked with Carr on media-related issues. The senator has argued the records raise questions about whether her hearing testimony was complete and whether FCC staff played a role in shaping commitments submitted as part of the merger review process. Neither the FCC nor Thumann Severs has publicly responded to those allegations. What Happens Next The Senate Commerce Committee is expected to consider Thumann Severs' nomination Wednesday. While Democrats are pressing for a delay, Republicans currently retain control of the committee and appear poised to move the nomination forward. If approved by the committee, the nomination would advance to the Senate floor before Democrats formally take control of the chamber in January.
news.summary: Democrats ask Texas Senator Ted Cruz to remove FCC nominee Danielle Thumann Severs from agenda.
news.author: Jennifer Radcliffe

news.title: Trump Navy Goon Makes Damning Admission About U.S. Missiles
news.text:
Trump’s hand-picked nominee for Navy Secretary revealed that the U.S. has been using expired munitions during the Iran war. 

On Tuesday, Hung Cao, a retired Navy captain who has served as acting secretary of the Navy since April, told the Senate Armed Services Committee that the military had been recoding and firing expired munitions during its war with Iran. His admission came despite President Donald Trump repeatedly dismissing reports that the conflict was depleting U.S. weapons stockpiles.

Cao, 55, said the military has been able to “recode” expired munitions to restore their functionality. The acting secretary drew an analogy about stale bread to explain the process. 

“I came from a poor family,” Cao told the senators. “Bread, things like bread doesn’t expire,” he added. “You just rub some water on the microwave for 15 seconds and it’s good to go. And so for some of these munitions, we recoded them, and so we’re able to shoot off the expired munitions.”

The Navy has the capability to revive expired munitions, though a portion of the missiles retain technical issues, The Wall Street Journal reports.

The Journal said that the U.S. used refurbished Tomahawk missiles during last year’s strikes on Islamic militants in Nigeria, but that several of the missiles were found intact in civilian areas. 

Cao’s testimony ran counter to the narrative Trump has been building about the U.S. military’s arsenal since the war began nearly nine months ago. 

In August, the New York Times reported that the military’s stockpiles of missiles and air-defense were dwindling after months of bombardment of Iran. At the time, chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell rejected the report.

“Everything required to strike at the time and place of the president’s choosing,” Parnell told the Times. 

Trump also repeatedly pushed back against reports of weapons shortages.

“The U.S. has massive amounts of “munitions,” especially of certain types,” he wrote on Truth Social in August. “Additionally, large amounts are being manufactured and shipped to the U.S. as needed. Defense companies are building the largest number of plants and factories in our country’s history. The “leakers” of these treasonous statements are being hunted down. Long term jail sentences will be sought.”

Later that day, Trump told reporters in the Oval Office the U.S. had “a virtual unlimited supply” of missiles. 

In an October interview with Time magazine, Trump dismissed reports of munitions shortages as “mostly fake news,” while acknowledging that supplies of some ammunition were “a little bit lower.” 

The White House did immediately not respond to a request for comment.

news.title: Trump says US is expanding defence cooperation with Philippines
news.text:
US President Donald Trump told his Philippine counterpart Ferdinand Marcos Jr on Wednesday that Washington was expanding defence cooperation with its treaty ally and could also work with Manila on a major civilian nuclear energy project.

Trump, who is in Manila on a state visit before heading to China for the APEC summit, said Washington had increased military support for the Philippines, approving more than $5 billion in arms sales.

Cooperation on a potential Philippine civilian nuclear power project could further strengthen ties between the two allies, Trump said.

“For the Philippines to embrace American technology in its first modern nuclear project would underscore the strength of the important relationship, and we’re probably going to do something very big to do with nuclear,” Trump said.

Trump said the Philippines could also become a partner in a planned Alaska natural gas export project, adding that the two countries were discussing broader energy cooperation.

“The Philippines would be a very natural partner in this effort. We are working on that,” he said.

Trump also said he was not concerned about the situation in the disputed South China Sea and said the US alliance with the Philippines has never been better.

“I am not concerned at all. That’ll be taken care of,” he said.
news.summary: Trump said the Philippines could also become a partner in a planned Alaska natural gas export project

 Nvidia says no return for ousted CEO, reports revenue boom 







SAN FRANCISCO, United States (AFP)—United States (US) chip giant Nvidia on Tuesday ruled out any comeback for ousted CEO Jensen Huang, who was forced out in a spy scandal, and reported that it had doubled revenue in the third quarter to more than $115 billion, beating expectations.

Huang sought to be reinstated despite resigning last week over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, but his successor — interim CEO Colette Kress — said that it was now “business as usual” at the company as it charts a way ahead without him.

Harvey Jones, the chair of the company’s board, said in an earnings call that “the Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.”

Investors scoured the upbeat results for evidence that the artificial intelligence boom can withstand the Nvidia crisis, which highlighted a loophole allegedly exploited by Chinese companies.

“Our momentum is real. Nvidia is an exceptional technology leader, powered by the relentless innovation of our people,” Kress said in her first remarks since being appointed by the board last week.

She forecast stronger revenue growth of 75 per cent in next fiscal year, up from 70 per cent.

Huang’s bid on Tuesday to get his job back was the latest twist for the company at the center of an AI boom that has propelled markets to record highs and boosted global economic growth.

The recent upheaval has battered shares of Nvidia — which has lost $700 billion in market value since the scandal broke — and Huang is to be questioned by US lawmakers on December 1 over national security concerns.

A charismatic promoter of AI, his fall triggered immediate calls from Elon Musk and others for his return, and even President Donald Trump said he “would not mind” seeing Huang back at Nvidia, downplaying the espionage allegations.

– Battle over AI chips –

“Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” Huang said, hours before the earnings release.

“If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.”

As the spy scandal deepened, Washington on Monday announced new restrictions on AI chip exports, drawing condemnation from Beijing.

The new US export curbs and the wider Nvidia scandal risk casting a shadow over talks between Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, which starts this week in the Chinese city of Shenzhen.

Under Washington’s new rules, data centers anywhere in the world will need a US license to provide large volumes of computing power from advanced chips to companies headquartered in China, Macau or other countries under US arms embargoes.

The rules also require licenses to ship advanced chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil — countries the US Commerce Department says present a “higher-than-normal risk of diversion” of the chips.

The changes are a response to a loophole that allowed Chinese firms to rent AI computing power from data centers in Southeast Asia and elsewhere that run on US hardware not available for export to China.

While the loophole has been known to authorities, the revelation of Huang’s affair has drawn intense scrutiny to the practice.

His lover Alice Huang, who is not related to the 63-year-old, is a former executive of Megaspeed — a Singapore-based cloud computing firm under US criminal investigation for allegedly helping Chinese companies procure advanced Nvidia AI chips in circumvention of export controls.

Investors are watching for signs of whether Kress will slow Huang’s aggressive investment strategy, which saw him commit tens of billions of dollars to AI companies.

Huang on Tuesday sounded a note of contrition in his statement, saying “I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life.”

news.title: Pichwai painting, Katan Silk stole: PM Modi presents traditional handicrafts to Quad leaders
news.text: Digital Desk | Manila, Nov 18 (IANS) Prime Minister Narendra Modi presented exquisite Indian artworks and traditional handicrafts to leaders of Quad partner countries during his visit to the Philippines, showcasing India's rich cultural heritage, centuries-old artistic traditions and the craftsmanship of its skilled artisans. As part of the gift exchange, PM Modi presented a traditional Pichwai painting to US President Donald Trump. Originating in Nathdwara in Rajasthan, the Golden Pichwai painting is a renowned form of traditional Indian cloth art, recognised for its intricate detailing, vibrant colours and elaborate compositions. The artwork is created on finely prepared cloth using mineral pigments, complemented by delicate gold detailing. Its compositions feature traditional motifs such as lotuses, cows, trees and ornamental borders, reflecting the exceptional skill, patience and precision of the artisans who practise this centuries-old art form. The use of gold gives the painting a distinctive luminous finish and a regal appearance. Rooted in India's traditional artistic practices, Pichwai paintings have preserved the country's cultural heritage across generations while providing continued recognition and support to traditional artisan communities. To Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, PM Modi gifted a traditional Jaipur Blue Pottery artefact, another distinctive craft associated with Rajasthan's rich handicraft heritage. Jaipur Blue Pottery is a unique traditional art form that stands apart from conventional pottery because it is made using a quartz-based mixture rather than ordinary clay. This specialised composition gives the finished products a smooth, delicate and slightly translucent appearance. The craft is widely recognised for its glossy white surface, enhanced by striking cobalt-blue designs. Its decorative patterns include finely hand-painted floral motifs, birds, geometric designs and intricate ornamental borders, showcasing the artistic precision and creativity of local craftsmen. The distinctive colours and glossy finish of Jaipur Blue Pottery are achieved through a specialised glazing and firing process that has been refined and preserved by artisans over several generations. The traditional craft is used to create a wide range of products, including vases, plates, bowls, tiles and other decorative objects. These pieces are appreciated both for their practical use and their value as collectable works of traditional Indian art. Jaipur Blue Pottery reflects Rajasthan's distinctive cultural and artistic identity. The craft plays an important role in preserving traditional skills, sustaining local artisan communities and supporting livelihoods, while representing the continuity of India's rich handicraft traditions. For Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, PM Modi presented a Royal Blue Banarasi Katan Silk Stole, carefully placed in an elegant Sadheli box, symbolising India's enduring friendship, warmth and cultural respect towards Japan. Woven from fine Katan silk, the stole represents the centuries-old textile-making traditions of Banaras. The fabric features intricate motifs that reflect the precision, dedication, and exceptional craftsmanship passed down through generations of Banarasi weavers. Its royal blue colour adds to the elegance of the stole and symbolises dignity, wisdom and harmony. The carefully crafted textile showcases the richness of India's traditional weaving practices and the artistic skills of its handloom artisans. The gift also serves as a lasting symbol of mutual respect, goodwill and the longstanding friendship between India and Japan.

news.title: Mike Pence Calls Trump Admin's $50B Request for FAA a 'Tough Lift'
news.text: Mike Pence, President Donald Trump's vice president during his first term, said the administration's new ask of Congress to approve $50 billion in funding for the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is a "tough lift." While speaking with CNN's Kaitlan Collins Tuesday night, Pence was asked if Congress should give the Trump administration the funds. "I think that's a tough lift. I really do. To me, with $8 billion unspent...let's get to work...And let's also make sure that the FAA has the proper staffing in the days ahead." Pence's remarks come after Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy asked Congress for additional funding after a nationwide ground stop on Friday. The aviation halt disrupted millions of travelers heading into the weekend and affected college and professional sports. Duffy's request for an additional $50 billion quickly drew bipartisan pushback, with lawmakers demanding answers about what went wrong and previous allocated funding. Newsweek reached out to the White House on Tuesday night for comment. What To Know Collins asked Pence if he thought Trump was out front enough following the ground stop and slew of outages plaguing banks, tech companies along with a highly classified internal communications system used by the National Security Agency (NSA). "I always kind of welcome a calming voice in any president," Pence said. "But I do think that when you recognize that we have enemies in the world, and with the expanded impact of artificial intelligence and the capabilities of the countries I mentioned, most especially China, that the president would do well to also signal that we will find out what the cause of this was and we will ensure that there is no vulnerability to the American people from countries that may well wish us harm in the future." Pence later added that cyberattacks are a real thing and that is now the world we live in, whether it impacts corporate America or government infrastructure. "We've got to be prepared," Pence said. Trump was asked about the outages impacting numerous entities, including the FAA, on Tuesday saying, "It's life. When you're big and powerful and you have all the money, things like that happen. It's fine." Speaking to reporters on Tuesday, Secretary of State Marco Rubio also addressed the outages saying, "We have no indication, no evidence, and no reason to believe at all that any of these incidents are related to each other. ... We have zero evidence or any reason to believe that any of these isolated or individual instances have anything to do with nefarious actors." He said that the administration acknowledges that it is unsettling to see reports of outages across numerous companies. "We see no indication that these things are interrelated one event to the other, or that they're the work of malign actors," Rubio added. Speaking specifically about funding, Pence also told Collins that "I do know that in the Big Beautiful Bill there was $12 billion made available for FAA improvements...and they haven't spent it all and requesting more. But I would tell you having been alongside a president for four years, you have to be able to count on your people to execute the plan. Making sure that we've got the leadership at the FAA, leadership at the Department of Transportation that's going to lean all the way into this and make sure that we have stable communications at the Federal Aviation Administration." Pence said that Duffy was right to order the ground stop in an effort to put the safety of the American people first. Duffy Pushes Back on Funding Questions Addressing concerns about funds previously allocated to the FAA, Duffy told reporters that he pays for new equipment after receiving the new products. Duffy gave an example of radar systems being built in Kansas and Florida via contract for the FAA that he says have not been delivered yet. "When I receive them, I'll pay for them," Duffy said. "So, all the money hasn't left our account and gone to those who won in the contract, I only am going to pay when they deliver." He said all the money has been set aside to modernize the antiquated aviation equipment. "This has never been done, to be clear we are keeping planes safe in the sky, and we are switching out equipment, it's been a problem for decades," Duffy said. Meanwhile, Democratic Representative Suhas Subramanyam of Virginia pushed back on Duffy's request in a post to X on Tuesday night saying, "Secretary Duffy wants $50 billion from Congress but has barely spent the $12.5 billion we already gave him. All non-vital network maintenance should stop through 2026, and the FAA must stop firing critical staff. We need real solutions, not another blank check." FAA and Air Traffic Control System Issues The FAA is in the midst of a multibillion-dollar effort to overhaul an air traffic control system that still relies on aging technology, including floppy disks. The FAA said earlier this month that it plans to eliminate the floppy disks used to store weather and other critical information at more than 400 air traffic facilities nationwide by the end of 2028. The system is also grappling with a shortage of air traffic controllers as the agency works to replace aging infrastructure ahead of the busy holiday travel season. Congress approved $12.5 billion over five years in 2025 to modernize air traffic control systems. Last Friday, the White House and Transportation Department asked Congress for an additional $30.1 billion, including $10.1 billion for air traffic control modernization, $2 billion for control towers and $18 billion for airport projects, Reuters reported. Following the ground stop, Duffy said he now wants $50 billion. Newsweek’s reporters and editors used Martyn, our AI assistant, to produce this story. Learn more about Martyn here. Contact Newsweek editors on this story: Edward T. Cummins
news.summary: The funding request comes on the heels of an unprecedented nationwide ground stop and as other companies have reported outages.

news.title: 'I Love Our Country & Nvidia': Jensen Huang Says He'll Return If Board Wants Him, Chairman Rules Out Comeback
news.text: Jensen Huang has said he would be honoured to return as Nvidia CEO if the board decides it is in the company's best interest. Hours later, the board's chairman said directors do not intend to bring him back. Both Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones and interim CEO Colette Kress have confirmed that the board has decided not to reinstate Huang. Huang's statementIn a statement on X, Huang said he had seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia's employees, investors, business partners and customers for him to return. He said he would answer those calls if the board decided his return served shareholders, employees, the company and America. He also said he loves the country and the company. Recalling that he arrived in the United States 53 years ago, he called American citizenship one of the proudest moments of his life and said a company like Nvidia could not have been built anywhere else.Huang accepted responsibility for his conduct. He said he had not met the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia, had made serious mistakes in his personal life, and had created problems for the board that he deeply regrets. He said he is committed to cooperating with the board's independent investigation. He ended by thanking supporters and apologising to his family.Chairman shuts the doorNvidia's newly appointed board chair, Harvey Jones, addressed Huang's resignation on the company's third-quarter earnings call on Tuesday. He said the board unanimously accepted Huang's resignation and does not intend to reinstate him as CEO. Jones also said Huang had voluntarily resigned his positions as president, CEO and board member. “Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned his positions as president, CEO and board member. The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO. In addition, the board announced it was initiating a search for a permanent chief executive, and we have since retained Heidrick & Struggles to lead the search,” he said during the call.Jones and interim CEO Colette Kress later said they would not take questions about Huang.The search for a successorJones said the board is taking the search for a new CEO "very seriously" and is considering internal and external candidates. Nvidia has retained Heidrick & Struggles to lead the search. Kress said the company wants a new chief executive as quickly as possible but will not rush before finding the right person. She also said that, from a business perspective, it is "business as usual".Pressure from supportersHuang's supporters have been vocal since his exit. The "Stand With Jensen" open letter asks the board to bring him back while an independent investigation establishes the facts. Its signatories include Elon Musk and Travis Kalanick. Reports put the signature count at more than 178,000. Totals differ across outlets, and the campaign says signers' identities are self-reported and unverified. US President Donald Trump said he "would not mind" seeing Huang return.Signs of a splitThe picture inside the boardroom is less clear. The Financial Times reported that Huang is discussing a comeback with allies in Silicon Valley. Semafor, citing informed sources, reported that a few board members are still pushing for his return while others have begun narrowing the search for a successor. Nvidia and Huang's representatives declined to comment on that report, and it has not been independently confirmed.Scrutiny continuesHuang has agreed to testify before Congress next month, lawmakers said on Tuesday. Nvidia has also created a board committee on national security and trade compliance. Huang resigned on November 12, days after admitting in an email to staff that he had been unfaithful to his wife. Reports have linked him to a former Megaspeed executive suspected of being a Chinese intelligence asset, and to a relationship with an Nvidia employee.
news.author: Tasneem Kanchwala

news.title: APEC live: Russia's Putin, Malaysia's Anwar lob veiled critiques at US
news.text:
SHENZHEN -- Chinese President Xi Jinping is set to host leaders including U.S. counterpart Donald Trump and Russia's Vladimir Putin at this year's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum, showcasing his own country's technological prowess against a backdrop of cold and hot conflicts.

The proceedings in the southern tech hub of Shenzhen kicked off with a CEO Summit of business leaders on Tuesday, to be followed by an Economic Leaders' Meeting beginning Wednesday. On the sidelines, Xi and Trump are expected to have their third summit of the year as they seek to manage a fraught superpower rivalry.

As the Ukraine war drags on and tensions with Iran simmer, all eyes are on a trilateral summit between Xi, Trump and Putin that the White House has said will happen on Thursday. This prospect has drawn comparisons to the Yalta conference between the U.S., U.K. and Soviet Union to discuss the fate of postwar Europe in 1945.

Before departing for Asia on Monday, Trump told reporters that he might meet North Korean leader Kim Jong Un in China, a surprise announcement that could become another focal point of his visit.

Nikkei Asia is on the ground in Shenzhen to cover the meetings.

Further reading:

Here are the latest developments (Shenzhen time):

Wednesday, Nov. 18

11:30 a.m. Russian President Vladimir Putin piles on with implicit criticism of the U.S., saying that "former dominant powers" have tried to suppress the development of other countries.

"Economic domination and coercion are now a thing of the past," he says, praising nations that have preserved their own identities and independence and arguing that sanctions and tariffs have not held Russia back.

He hails Shenzhen as a "modern vibrant megacity" and a symbol of tech, economic and social transformation in China and Asia. The region, he says, is setting an example of a "more fair, democratic and equal world order."

11:15 a.m. Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim is the next to address business leaders after China's Xi. While praising the host several times, Anwar delivers thinly veiled criticism of the U.S., without naming it directly. He stresses the importance of free and open business activity, emphasizing, "You can't say in one voice [that you're] promoting trade and investment, but only to your country."

11:10 a.m. Stan Shih, the founder of computer maker Acer and Taiwan's representative to the APEC summit, says he will "actively" engage with other members in Shenzhen as he departs from Taipei, according to Reuters.

APEC is one of the few international organizations that includes Taiwan, which participates as "Chinese Taipei." The administration is sending Shih in lieu of President Lai Ching-te, who Beijing considers a "separatist" because he rejects its territorial claim to Taiwan.

Shih describes Taiwan as a "trustworthy" player in the region and an indispensable partner for the global technology and AI sectors. He vows to "show the international community Taiwan's strength and contributions."

"Taiwan will go with a smile," he says.

10:10 a.m. Xi addresses the APEC CEO Summit, his first time to do so in person since 2018 in Papua New Guinea. Positioning himself as an advocate for stability, he called for resolving differences through dialogue and for defending free and open trade. He is discussing the dilemmas economies face between being open or closed, between cooperation and division and between change or taking a conservative approach. "These are all questions of our time that we must answer," he said.

9:45 a.m. The second day of APEC proceedings is about to get underway. Putin landed in Shenzhen overnight, while Trump is expected to fly in later in the day, as is Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. A number of leaders, including Xi and Putin, are due to deliver speeches to business participants, with more bilateral mettings on the sidelines.

Tuesday, Nov. 17

5:30 p.m. Xi continues his day of meetings with visiting leaders, sitting down separately with Mexico's Claudia Sheinbaum, Peru's Keiko Fujimori and Chile's Jose Antonio Kast.

Mexico last year riled China by approving higher tariffs on countries with which it does not have trade deals, affecting hundreds of products. The move was widely seen as an effort to close a "back door" to the U.S.

Sheinbaum told Xi she is eager to step up cooperation with China in areas related to technology, agriculture, water, health and tourism, according to Reuters.

4:30 p.m. Speculation that North Korean leader Kim Jong Un could appear at APEC and meet with Trump continues to grow. Russia's Interfax news agency has cited the Kremlin as saying that Putin could also meet Kim if he shows up in Shenzhen, adding weight to the prospect of a Kim visit.

Shortly before he departed the U.S. for Asia, Trump himself suggested that a meeting with Kim could happen. Trump met Kim three times during his first presidency and has expressed interest in a reunion.

3:30 p.m. BYD Chairman and President Wang Chuanfu says on a panel that the electric carmaker's Thailand and Indonesia plants have created 6,000 local jobs each and nearly all of its employees at the factories are local hires.

"Our goal is not merely to export Chinese technology globally; we also aim to generate local employment and tax revenue, fostering mutually beneficial cooperation and win-win outcomes," he said.

Wang added that its Thailand factory sources just over half of components domestically.

His comments come as a rush of Chinese vehicle exports stokes trade tensions with some partner economies.

2:00 p.m. Papua New Guinea Prime Minister James Marape has assured Xi that Taiwan no longer operates in his country. PNG pushed for the closure of Taipei's representative office in its capital, Port Moresby, and Taiwan announced earlier this month that it would indeed shut down the mission.

Marape told Xi that he hopes the move "assists you in your efforts for reunification," referring to China's claim to Taiwan, which the administration in Taipei rejects.

Taiwan had been a major buyer of gas from PNG, but said it would halt spot purchases in reaction to the closure. China, in turn, committed to increasing its purchases.

12:30 p.m. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said there is now "greater predictability and stability" in his country's ties with China, as he met Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen. Xi said that since the two leaders agreed to promote a strategic partnership back in January, exchanges and cooperation between China and Canada have fully resumed.

Carney's visit to Beijing in January thawed a relationship that had been severely strained in recent years, especially after the 2018 detention of Huawei executive Meng Wanzhou in Canada and the subsequent jailing of two Canadians on espionage charges -- all of whom were eventually released.

A statement released by Carney's office about Tuesday's meeting says that Canada "has recalibrated our relationship with China -- strategically, pragmatically, and decisively." It also says the two sides agreed to extend and expand a preliminary agreement to address trade issues, opening up greater access to the Chinese market for Canada's farmers and seafood harvesters and securing more tariff relief for about 400 million Canadian dollars ($280 million) worth of exports.

The statement also mentions a slew of other initiatives to boost trade, e-commerce, educational exchanges and air travel.

11:30 a.m. Trump's Air Force One made a refueling stop in Alaska before a layover in the Philippines, where Manila is hosting ASEAN leaders and related summits.

Before leaving Washington, Trump said he might meet North Korean leader Kim Jong Un in China. The hermit nation is not a member of APEC and South Korean officials played down the possibility of such a meeting, Yonhap News Agency reported on Nov. 11.

Trump's planned attendance at APEC contrasts with last year's summit in Gyeongju, South Korea, when he met Xi Jinping in Busan and secured a trade truce but left before the main agenda began. His Shenzhen engagement signals an effort to keep ties with Xi on track ahead of next month's G20 Summit in Miami, where they are expected to meet again.

9:30 a.m. Beijing has yet to formally respond to Washington's latest move to tighten China's access to advanced artificial intelligence chips through overseas data centers. Vice Premier He Lifeng raised concerns over U.S. restrictions on China in a phone call earlier this month.

The broader AI boom is also rattling markets. Shenzhen's tech-heavy ChiNext Index sank 4.4% on Monday to a nearly 16-month low, led by steep losses among suppliers to AI data centers. U.S. stocks also fell sharply ahead of Nvidia's earnings on Tuesday.

9:00 a.m. Foreign leaders are trickling into Shenzhen. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum and Papua New Guinea Prime Minister James Marape arrived on Monday, according to Chinese media.

The leaders are expected to hold bilateral meetings with Xi on Tuesday, according to media reports. Carney is visiting China for the second time this year. In January, he met with Xi and lowered Canada's tariff wall on Chinese electric vehicles by setting up an import quota. Among the topics expected to be discussed during his visit to Shenzhen is Chinese investment into Canada's auto sector.

Trade tensions loom over Sheinbaum's visit, after she raised import tariffs on cars, textiles, appliances and other items from countries without free trade agreements with Mexico, including China. In addition to meeting Xi, she is expected to speak at the CEO Summit on Tuesday.

news.title: Mary Peltola Defeats Incumbent Republican in Alaska Senate Race
news.text:
Her victory puts the Senate balance of power at 56-44, in favor of Democrats, who secured control of both chambers of Congress in the midterms as the American public appeared to reject President Donald Trump amid concerns about the Iran war, inflation, and more. In the eight Senate contests that appeared least predictable, Democrats won all of them, and they even won in Mississippi too, where election forecasters had rated the race as likely Republican.

Read More: The Democratic Wins No Election Forecaster Expected

The race was dominated by controversy over allegations that independent runner Dan J. Sullivan, a retired teacher, was a spoiler candidate, intended to confuse Alaskans and draw votes away from the incumbent Republican Senator with the same first and last name.

Despite protests from Trump, Republicans were unsuccessful in trying to remove the second Sullivan from the ballot. A federal judge on Nov. 1 dismissed a lawsuit by the Trump Administration that sought to delay certifying the results in Alaska if the incumbent Republican lost the race. "The United States provides no workable plan as to how it proposes to segregate ballots cast for Daniel J. Sullivan on Election Day and then conduct a court-ordered unspecified 'investigation' of those ballots in a manner that would preserve voter secrecy,” ruled District Judge Sharon Gleason, referring to the Oct. 22 lawsuit.
news.summary: Democratic challenger Mary Peltola triumphed over Republican Sen. Dan S. Sullivan, rounding out a controversy-plagued race and handing the Democratic caucus a 56-44 majority in the Senate.
news.author: Callum Sutherland

news.title: US Navy Chief Blasted Over "Minimising" Mental Health Strain Of Iran War
news.text: Democratic lawmakers tore into President Donald Trump's acting head of the Navy on Tuesday, accusing him of being a Trump "yes man" on the Iran war and downplaying its toll on sailors' mental health after eight suicide attempts on an aircraft carrier.The contentious hearing during the waning days of the Republican-led Senate could be a preview of what's to come when Democrats take control in January after victories in midterm elections earlier this month.Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao, who is seeking to win Senate confirmation to keep the job, did not directly respond to some of the toughest questions before the Senate Armed Services Committee about the Iran war. Those included the cost of the US naval blockade on Iran and the damage to the Navy's headquarters in the Middle East after attacks by Iran.But it was his defense of Navy conditions on board the Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group and his praise for the Navy's mental health crisis response that drew the fiercest criticism from Democratic senators.Senator Kirsten Gillibrand, a Democrat from New York, asked him about a sailor who went overboard."Senator, that sailor was not trying to kill himself and he admitted that," Cao told her, saying he used a life preserver.Gillibrand responded: "What was he trying to do? Swim to Guam?""I think you are minimising what mental health strain is on these service members," Gillibrand replied, adding she thought Cao's response was "inhumane" and "inadequate."Republican Representative Rob Wittman from Virginia extolled Cao as he introduced him as "a remarkable American story," a refugee from Vietnam who served in the Navy for 25 years, including in Iraq, Afghanistan and Somalia, retiring at the rank of captain.Cao, whose son is in the Marine Corps, told the committee he wanted the job to ensure sailors "don't go to war the way we did" in Iraq, without armored vehicles or enough body armor.Senator Angus King, an independent from Maine who caucuses with the Democrats, said he was moved by Cao's personal story but said it was also ironic as Trump's administration cuts refugee admissions."Today, your family wouldn't be let in the country," King said.Quantity For Quality?Republican Senator Tom Cotton of Arkansas dismissed talk of poor conditions on Navy ships. "If the picture painted by the Democrats were so bleak, would the Navy have reached its recruiting goals three months early?" he asked.Cao responded, "Senator, we would not be there."Senator Jack Reed, a Democrat from Rhode Island, pointed to data he said showed most new Navy recruits required waivers from standard qualification requirements - including on issues like mental health."Are you sort of sacrificing quality for quantity?" Reed asked, to a denial from Cao.Cao will himself require a waiver to be confirmed to the job, since he only retired from the Navy in 2021 - putting him below the required seven-year cooling-off period to become its civilian leader.Voter anger over the Iran war, which has settled into an effective stalemate focused on securing the Strait of Hormuz, helped Democrats win control of Congress. A Reuters/Ipsos poll published last week found a majority of Americans want the newly elected Democratic-majority US Congress to act to end the war with Iran once and for all.The Navy has played a critical role in the war, imposing a punishing naval blockade on Iran and helping deliver strikes on Iranian territory. This week, a third aircraft carrier entered Middle East waters, though officials say it is expected to replace one of the two carriers present.While the US military points to the heavy toll imposed on Iran's conventional military, and its ability to help escort tankers through the Strait of Hormuz past Iranian shores, the Pentagon has not yet explained how it sees the conflict ending.Senator Tammy Duckworth, a Democrat from Illinois, asked whether Cao ever stood up to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over the war."Senator, it's not within my purview to do that," Cao said.Duckworth responded sharply: "It is within your purview!""This is a failure of leadership by President Trump and the unqualified yes-men he's installed, and it sounds like you want to be one of those," she said.(Except for the headline, this story has not been edited by NDTV staff and is published from a syndicated feed.)
news.summary: Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao, who is seeking to win Senate confirmation to keep the job, did not directly respond to some of the toughest questions before the Senate Armed Services Committee about the Iran war.
news.author: Reuters

news.title: China makes call for free and open trade in his opening speech for APEC summit
news.text:
Today Chinese President Xi Jinping just championed ‘free and open trade’, something that would not rely on investment barriers, in his opening speech at an Asia-Pacific summit he met his US and Russian counterparts.

It is important to mention that Xi's remarks came after Washington announced further restrictions on China's access to advanced AI chips from companies such as which could further complicate its already ‘fragile’ trade truce with Beijing and China has pledged to retaliate.

Xi’s exact words to the audience came right after posing a series of rhetorical questions on how the Asia Pacific should respond to a changing world. He claimed, “We must firmly uphold the rules-based multilateral trading system with the World Trade ⁠Organization at its core, support free and open trade and investment, maintain the stability and smooth operation of global industrial and supply chains.”

Western trade partners however have criticised China for running annual trade surpluses, in an excess of $1 trillion, through policies that support its manufacturing sector at the expense of its consumers.

While Beijing believes its growth model is ‘appropriate’ for an economy still catching ‌up ⁠with the world's richest, Washington, Brussels and many others claim they are ‘concerned’ about China's supply chain dominance, especially since it provides the country with geopolitical leverage and some worry its policies threaten their industries and jobs.

Moreover, Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation CEOs summit will convene on Thursday. Xi was at the opening, in the southern Chinese tech hub of Shenzhen.

Russian President Vladimir Putin landed overnight, (after Ukraine destroyed the vital Kerch road bridge linking Crimea to Russia in a major blow to his four-year-old war.) ⁠While US President Donald Trump was due to arrive later on Wednesday (after concluding meetings with Southeast Asian and other regional leaders in Manila.)

The high-stakes talks tomorrow aim to touch bas on the Middle East conflict, as well as on other points such as trade, AI and nuclear weapons also on the agenda.

news.title: What PM Modi gifted to Asean, Quad leaders during Manila visit
news.text: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi presented a range of traditional Indian artworks and handicrafts to world leaders during his visit to Manila, the Philippines, offering gifts that showcased the country's diverse regional craftsmanship, textile traditions and cultural heritage.The gifts included a Golden Pichwaai painting from Rajasthan for US President Donald Trump, a traditional Kashmiri silk carpet for Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr and a Chola bronze sculpture for Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto.PM Modi also presented a Dokra artwork boat to Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet, Bidriware silver inlay vases to Myanmar and Brunei, a royal blue Banarasi silk stole to Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, and a Jaipur blue pottery artefact to Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese.The presents drew on traditional art forms and crafts from different parts of India, including Rajasthan, Kashmir, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh and the Deccan region.What Modi gifted to Trump, Marcos and other leadersUS President Donald Trump: Golden Pichwaai paintingPM Modi gifted Trump a Golden Pichwaai painting from Nathdwara in Rajasthan. The traditional cloth-painting art is known for its intricate detailing, luminous colours and elaborate compositions.Created on finely prepared cloth using mineral pigments and gold detailing, Pichwaai paintings feature motifs such as lotuses, cows and trees, along with ornamental borders. Their golden finish gives the artwork a distinctive regal appearance.Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr: Kashmiri silk carpetThe Philippine President received a traditional Kashmiri silk carpet, a hand-knotted craft admired for its sheen, soft texture, intricate designs and durability.Made from fine silk, the carpets involve thousands of knots tied by skilled artisans. Some take months or even years to complete. Their designs often draw inspiration from Kashmir's natural beauty, featuring floral patterns, chinar leaves and geometric motifs.Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto: Chola bronze sculpturePM Modi presented a traditional Chola bronze sculpture to Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto. The art form flourished between the ninth and thirteenth centuries under the Chola dynasty in South India.The sculptures are made using the traditional lost-wax casting technique, known as Madhuchista Vidhana. Each piece is individually handcrafted, making it unique.Known for their anatomical precision, graceful forms and expressive details, Chola bronzes also offer insights into the clothing, jewellery, hairstyles and artistic traditions of the period. They represent Tamil Nadu's metallurgical skills and artistic heritage.Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim: Silver worked urliPM Modi gifted Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim a traditional silver worked urli, a decorative Indian vessel adorned with intricate silver embellishments that showcase the skill of the country's metalworkers.Traditionally filled with water and decorated with floating flowers, the urli symbolises purity, prosperity, hospitality and harmony.Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet: Dokra artwork boatCambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet received a traditional Dokra artwork boat. The metal craft is made using the lost-wax casting technique, a tradition dating back more than 4,000 years.The handcrafted piece depicts a boat carrying figures and birds, reflecting community life and harmony with nature. Each artwork is individually modelled in wax before being cast in metal.The boat symbolises unity, cooperation, resilience and collective progress. The craft also preserves traditional skills and supports artisan livelihoods.Myanmar and Brunei: Bidriware silver inlay vasesPM Modi gifted Bidriware silver inlay vases from Bidar, Karnataka, to Myanmar and Sultan Haji Hassanal Bolkiah of Brunei.Bidriware is a traditional metal craft made from a zinc-and-copper alloy and decorated with intricate pure silver inlay. Artisans engrave patterns, insert silver wire and treat the surface to create its characteristic deep black finish, which contrasts with the silver designs.The floral and geometric motifs draw inspiration from the architectural heritage of Bidar Fort. The craft has a Geographical Indication (GI) tag and represents the artistic traditions of the Deccan region.Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi: Banarasi Katan silk stoleJapanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi received a royal blue Banarasi Katan silk stole presented in a Sadheli box.Woven from fine Katan silk, the stole showcases the centuries-old textile traditions of Banaras. Its intricate motifs reflect the craftsmanship and precision of generations of weavers.The royal blue colour symbolises dignity, wisdom and harmony, while the presentation in a Sadheli box represents India's warmth and cultural esteem.Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese: Jaipur blue pottery artefactPM Modi gifted Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese a traditional Jaipur blue pottery artefact from Rajasthan.The craft is known for its glossy white surface and luminous cobalt-blue designs. Its pieces feature hand-painted floral patterns, birds, geometric motifs and decorative borders.Lao Prime Minister Sonexay Siphandone: Rose quartz elephant with gold workPM Modi gifted Lao Prime Minister Sonexay Siphandone a rose quartz elephant with gold work, a decorative craft associated with Rajasthan's stone-carving centres, particularly Jaipur.The artwork is carved from natural rose quartz and polished to bring out its soft, translucent sheen. It is then decorated with intricate hand-painted gold detailing, floral motifs and traditional ornamental designs.Combining gemstone carving with miniature painting, the elephant symbolises strength, wisdom, dignity and royal grandeur in Indian tradition. Its gilded detailing reflects India's heritage of luxury handicrafts and royal decorative arts.Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul: Rogan art paintingThai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul received a traditional Rogan art painting from Kutch, Gujarat. Practised by a handful of artisan families in Nirona village, Rogan art is a rare, centuries-old textile painting tradition.The technique uses a thick, elastic paint prepared by boiling castor oil and mixing it with natural pigments. Artisans create intricate designs freehand on fabric using a slender metal stylus. The cloth is then folded to transfer a symmetrical mirror image onto the other half.Traditionally used in bridal trousseaus and festive attire, Rogan art is known for its intricate patterns, geometric precision and craftsmanship. It represents Kutch's cultural heritage and the ingenuity of its artisans.Timor-Leste Prime Minister Kay Rala Xanana Gusmão: Handcrafted agate bowlPM Modi gifted Timor-Leste Prime Minister Kay Rala Xanana Gusmão a handcrafted agate bowl from Khambhat, Gujarat. Made from agate, a semi-precious gemstone, each bowl has distinctive natural bands, colours and textures, making every piece unique.Khambhat has been a centre of agate processing and stone carving for centuries. Skilled artisans carefully cut, shape and polish the stone to create decorative and functional objects.Vietnamese Prime Minister Le Minh Hung: Traditional Indian leather wall hangingVietnamese Prime Minister Le Minh Hung received a traditional Indian leather wall hanging, a handcrafted decorative artwork rooted in the country's folk-art heritage.Artisans soften and stretch treated leather before creating intricate designs through perforation, embossing and painting. The artworks feature floral, geometric and wildlife motifs, often made using natural vegetable dyes.Rooted in rural traditions and passed down through generations, the craft reflects regional artistic styles and storytelling. It also helps preserve traditional skills and support artisan livelihoods.PM Modi's two-day visit to ManilaThe gifts were presented during PM Modi's November 16-17 visit to the Philippines, where he attended the 23rd Asean-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit. He also participated in a Quad leaders' meeting with Trump, Takaichi and Albanese.During the visit, India and Asean adopted a joint statement on cooperation in disaster management. The two sides also agreed to strengthen early warning systems, share satellite data, conduct joint simulation exercises and promote the use of artificial intelligence in disaster risk assessment and response coordination.PM Modi announced several initiatives to deepen India's engagement with the region, including a maritime cooperation plan, a joint cyber forensics training programme, technical exchanges on nuclear energy, a space hackathon and cooperation on critical minerals.Other announcements included youth and start-up initiatives, enhanced scholarships for Asean students at Nalanda University and free e-visas for tourists from Asean countries.Get the latest India News and Live updates. news.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi presented various traditional Indian artworks to leaders during his visit to Manila. These gifts highlighted India's rich cultural heritage and regional craftsmanship throughout the nation. Notable gifts included a Golden Pichwaai painting for the US President and a Kashmiri silk carpet for the Philippine President. The visit also included discussions on regional cooperation and disaster management initiatives.

news.title: Foreign Applicants To US Colleges Rise By 9% This Fall, 17% More From India
news.text: International applicants to US colleges this fall jumped by 9% from the same time last year, reversing a steep decline spurred by President Donald Trump's crackdown on student visa holders, according to data from Common App. The rebound was driven largely by a resurgence of applicants from Europe and Asia, which increased 15% and 9%, respectively. Applicants from India, which sends more international students to the US than any other country, rose by 17%, recovering from a 14% decrease last year.Other countries saw a similar change in tide: Applicants from Ghana rose 21% after a 43% drop last year, and the number from Pakistan increased by 41% after a 10% dip last fall.It's a surprising turnaround as the Trump administration continues to try to curb the number of foreign students and scholars on US campuses. In the past six months, federal officials have placed a four-year limit on student visa duration, proposed a $100,000 fee to participate in a popular postgraduate work program and investigated colleges including Harvard and Stanford over their foreign scholars and PhD students. Meanwhile, international enrollment has fallen precipitously. The number of new students in the US from abroad fell by 15% this fall, according to official data released Monday. And the number of domestic applicants remained flat this fall, Common App data shows, compared with a 7% rise last year.Data in the Common App report was only collected up to Nov. 1, and many students don't apply to college until closer to the January deadlines. An uptick in applications also won't necessarily translate to an enrollment rebound, as students who commit to attending school in the US are struggling with a more stringent visa approval process. Still, the increase bucks a dramatic downward trend that began early in the last application cycle, and is an upbeat signal for the colleges that rely on international students' tuition dollars and research contributions. Other recent developments may further encourage international applicants. On Monday, a federal judge struck down the Department of Homeland Security's rule limiting student visa holders' stay to four years. And the overwhelming Democratic victory in this month's midterm elections could stymie legislative efforts to further restrict student visa holders from entering the country. Growth in international applicants this fall was largely focused on the most selective institutions in the country. Schools with the lowest acceptance rates saw a 35% rise in international applicants, whereas those that accept more than three-quarters of applicants saw international interest decline slightly."The bounce-back in international applicants and the increase in applications to selective institutions appear to be related," said Walter Herring, Common App's director of applied analytics and research. The connection points to a glut of interest in a tiny pool of hyper-competitive schools with very few available seats. That could make it less likely that the application uptick translates to an enrollment rebound across American higher education. The Common App only collects data on undergraduate applicants. Graduate and doctoral programs, which have seen the most precipitous declines in international students - and enroll a disproportionate number of them - are not represented.(Except for the headline, this story has not been edited by NDTV staff and is published from a syndicated feed.)
news.summary: Applicants from India, which sends more international students to the US than any other country, rose by 17%, recovering from a 14% decrease last year.

news.title: Putin expects major benefits from upcoming meeting with Xi, Trump
news.text:
SHENZHEN /China/, November 18. /TASS/. Russian head of state Vladimir Putin said he sees considerable potential benefits in his upcoming trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and US leader Donald Trump.

He stressed the need for dialogue and pointed to APEC as an example of how to organize it well.

"APEC offers ample opportunities for constructive dialogue at all levels, especially among the leaders of major economies. They can sit down together to exchange views, resolve any political, economic or security disagreements between countries by seeking compromises and balancing interests, and work together to strengthen the foundations for sustainable development worldwide," Putin said.

"That’s why I see considerable potential benefits in the upcoming trilateral meeting between the leaders of Russia, China and the United States, which is scheduled to take place on the sidelines of the APEC summit," he added.

news.title: Former hegemons resist just world order – Putin (VIDEO)
news.text:
Russian President Vladimir Putin has accused former global hegemons of resisting the emergence of a more equitable world order, arguing that they are attempting to hold back successful developing nations rather than adapting to shifting economic realities.

Addressing the APEC CEO Summit in Shenzhen, China, on Wednesday, Putin said the global economy had undergone a “tectonic shift,” with the Asia-Pacific region emerging as the planet’s leading technological hub. Asian economies, he argued, have made a giant leap from being the “world’s factory” to becoming major drivers of innovation.

Over the past 35 years, the share of developing and emerging-market economies in global output has nearly doubled, rising from 35% in 1990 to 61% in 2026, according to the Russian leader.

“It was here, in the Asia-Pacific region, that the fundamental changes now spreading across the world like waves first originated,” Putin said.

The regional economic model demonstrates how a “fairer, more democratic and equitable world order” is taking shape, he argued, with traditional hierarchical structures giving way to new horizontal relationships between nations.

“However, these inevitable changes, this shift in the center of gravity of the global economic balance, are not always adequately perceived,” Putin said.

Instead of adapting to these opportunities, former hegemons, contrary to the logic of fair competition and sometimes, frankly speaking, even against their own interests, seek to restrain the development of those demonstrating success and progress.

The Russian president argued that these policies have fueled growing interest among Asia-Pacific nations in strengthening their sovereignty.

Putin also criticized European countries for failing to adapt to the loss of access to Russian markets and cheap energy resources, claiming that the EU is losing its economic standing and potential.

Addressing Western sanctions, he described Russia as the world’s “record holder” for the number of restrictions imposed against it, but insisted that the country had successfully weathered the pressure. He noted that Russia’s GDP has grown by more than 10% over the past three years, while its public debt remains among the world’s lowest, at around 17% of GDP.

Putin also argued that Moscow had never voluntarily abandoned the dollar or euro, and that those who restricted Russia’s access to the currencies had ultimately “punished themselves.”

Putin arrived in Shenzhen early Wednesday for the APEC summit, which will also bring together Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump. The three leaders are scheduled to hold landmark trilateral talks on Thursday, focusing on nuclear arms control, international security, and the conflicts in Ukraine and Iran. Putin is also expected to hold separate bilateral talks with Xi and Trump.
news.summary:
The Russian president has accused once-dominant powers of seeking to suppress emerging economies in a speech to business leaders in China
