news.title: Trump heads to China, betting on unscripted diplomacy with Xi and Putin
news.text: China: President Donald Trump departs Wednesday for China, where he will participate in a historic trilateral meeting with that country's president, Xi Jinping, and Russian leader Vladimir Putin at a time when much of the world has been on edge because of the wars in Ukraine and Iran and the transformations wrought by artificial intelligence.The president has signalled that he wants to take an improvised approach to his time in Shenzhen, China, the skyscraper-filled tech hub that is hosting world leaders for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. It's a bet that his unscripted brand of diplomacy based on personal relationships can create some kind of legacy to reshape world affairs during his final two years in the White House..Trump said he plans to talk with Xi and Putin about limiting nuclear weapons and bringing an end to the war in Ukraine, which began in 2022 with Russia's invasion. Analysts are not expecting substantive breakthroughs, despite the unprecedented nature of the meeting.Before the trip, Trump's aides had told reporters that the war in Ukraine would not be part of the trilateral meeting. Still, the president said on Tuesday that the deaths of tens of thousands of Russian troops every month had created an opening to resolve the conflict."I think it's very close to getting it done," Trump said. "We're going to have a good meeting on that.".Trump also teased the possibility of a private meeting with Putin and a separate sit-down with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, though neither event has been confirmed beyond the US president's own musings."I don't know, but I would. If it's available, I would do that," Trump said Tuesday about talking on the sidelines with Putin.Trump said "We'll see what happens" on the prospect of meeting with Kim, whose nuclear arsenal is a threat to the US and its allies in Japan and South Korea. Trump said the North Korean leader would like to meet..Trump may have a reunion with Imelda Marcos.The US president starts his day in the Philippine capital, Manila, where he may have a short reunion with Imelda Marcos, the former first lady, whose son is now president. Trump is having lunch with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr at the Malacanang Presidential Palace.Famed for her lavish shoe collection, Imelda Marcos knew Trump decades ago through the New York City party scene. During the 1986 "People Power" uprising, her husband, Ferdinand, was ousted as the Philippines' strongman leader. The meeting with the now 97-year-old former first lady depends on her doctors' approval..Trump on Tuesday met with leaders of the Quad alliance in Manila, signed a trade statement with Thailand and was feted at a formal dinner with Southeast Asian leaders.Trump plans to depart in the afternoon for Shenzhen, and he expressed excitement about the arrival ceremony that awaits him."I am the guest of President Xi and I hear we're going to have quite a landing," he told reporters. "It's going to be a beautiful thing."The US president on Thursday will participate in the APEC summit and then hold his meeting with Xi and Putin, before then returning to the US..What's on the agenda for Trump's meetings with Xi and Putin.The prospect of Trump meeting with two of America's largest geopolitical rivals has been a source of concern as the US president has been less welcoming of historic allies such as Canada and NATO partners in Europe.His tariffs that were intended to curb China's trade surplus have done little to stop the progress of the world's dominant manufacturer, which for the second straight year will have exported USD 1 trillion more in goods than what it imported.On Tuesday, Xi met with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and they agreed to further reduce tariffs on each other's goods. Carney has cultivated tighter economic ties with China and the European Union in response to strains in Canada's relationship with Trump, who at times has said he wants to make the country America's 51st state..Questions about how to handle AI also loom over the summit. The technology is viewed as key to unlocking faster economic growth, but its rapid development has meant it poses national security risks and could be beyond human control.Trump's close tech industry ally Jensen Huang was recently removed as the CEO of Nvidia after he admitted to an affair with a woman alleged to be an agent of the Chinese government. Beijing has denied that she was a spy, yet the affair raised concerns about how China has been able to access Nvidia computer chips to develop its own AI models that are competing with the US.When asked this week why the US had not been more aggressive in cutting off China's access to advanced computer chips, Trump said there were differences of opinion inside his administration and that "We have a very good relationship with China, and you don't want to insult them.".Both Russia and China have provided support to Iran after Trump launched a war there in late February to halt that country's development of nuclear weapons. The war has pushed up inflation and slowed global growth as energy prices have swung in response to each escalation and every pause in the conflict.Trump has said he intends to talk about the Iran war and efforts to reduce nuclear weapons. He said he does not plan to bring up Taiwan, a self-governing island that China claims as its own. Taiwan is the leading manufacturer of advanced computer chips, including those designed by US companies.Still, Trump expects that Xi will push him on Taiwan's sovereignty."I'm sure he'll raise it," Trump said. “I won't have to raise it."
news.author: Associated Press

news.title: Xi and Putin Set to Meet Ahead of Historic Trump Summit in China
news.text: SHENZHEN, China: Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin were set to meet Wednesday, a day ahead of a historic three-way summit with Donald Trump in Shenzhen. Thursday's trilateral has triggered fears that the three powerful men could decide the fate of Ukraine over the heads of Kyiv and Europe, and seek to carve up the world into 21st-century spheres of influence. Washington had signalled Ukraine was not expected to be addressed -- something Xi vehemently sees as not China's problem -- before Trump said that it would. China has said only that the leaders would hold "in-depth exchanges on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations" on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting. Also up for discussion is the Iran war and nuclear disarmament, according to Washington, after a US-Russia bilateral treaty on atomic weapons expired in February. Beijing has long maintained that the US and Russia should reduce their giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its smaller stockpile. - In from the cold - Putin, who arrived in Shenzhen early Wednesday, has been shunned by the West since launching Europe's worst conflict since World War II with his 2022 attack on Ukraine. Xi and Putin were both due to address the APEC gathering before discussing energy and finance and then -- in a smaller format -- foreign policy including Ukraine and North Korea, Russian officials said. Xi on Wednesday called for greater international cooperation on AI and free trade. "Starting by lowering tariffs, expanding access and exploring regulations and management standards, China will conduct deep-seated reform," Xi said. - Kim incoming? - Trump was on Wednesday still in the Philippines where a day earlier he met fellow leaders of the Quad -- Australia, Japan and India. He said he was eyeing one-on-one talks with Putin and possibly North Korea's Kim Jong Un at his next stop in Shenzhen. He added that Kim "would like" to meet in China, hours after Beijing said it had no information about an encounter between the two. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Wednesday stopped short of confirming the meeting with Kim. "If we have a problem with North Korea, the only way we're ever going to solve it is if we engage with them," Rubio said in Manila. Trump's Quad meeting at the 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit was the security alliance's first since his January 2025 return to power. The grouping is broadly aimed at counterbalancing China's regional influence. Trump's visit to the Philippines saw protests by around 2,000 people carrying banners reading "Trump out now" and "Reject Pax Silica" -- a reference to a US supply chain initiative. - Tariffs, chips and rare earths - While ASEAN leaders grappled with a raft of regional issues, the spectre of Trump's ongoing tariff blitz has loomed large. Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Monday slammed what he called a "countercurrent of unilateralism and protectionism" while touting Beijing's own expanding trade with the bloc. Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Canada's Mark Carney sang a similar tune on trade, with both explicitly citing a need to wean themselves off dependence on the US market. On Tuesday, a combative Trump showed no let-up in his trade war with Beijing, saying the United States would catch China in rare earths production "within 10 months". Hours before Trump touched down in Manila, Washington announced new rules on the transfer of advanced AI chips, a move that could potentially rankle ASEAN members. Companies shipping high-end chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia will now require a special licence, as the countries were said to represent a "higher-than-normal risk of diversion". Singapore responded by saying it was now exploring ways to facilitate "trusted access" for firms based in the city-state. - Pax Silica - Trump was set to meet Philippine leader Ferdinand Marcos at the presidential palace on Wednesday before heading to Shenzhen. Aimed at countering China's dominance in semiconductors and rare earths, the initiative has been the focus of months of protests in the Philippines as it threatens to displace Indigenous families. "We are gathered here today to call for the stop of Pax Silica and to save the lands of the Filipino people," Mariposa, a 21-year-old drag queen, told AFP at Tuesday's protest while wearing a long black cape emblazoned with the words "Pax Silica Sashay Away!"

news.title: ​Nvidia Board Has No Plans to Reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, Says Chairman Harvey Jones Despite Backing From Donald Trump and Elon Musk
news.text:

​Huang Cites ‘Outpouring’ of Support: In his first social media statement since stepping down, Huang acknowledged making “serious mistakes” in his personal life but claimed employees, investors, business partners, and customers had urged him to return—adding that he would answer the call if the board deemed it in the best interest of shareholders, the company, and the United States.

​Trump & Musk Back Reinstatement: Huang’s bid for a comeback has drawn vocal support from Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk as well as President Donald Trump, who has reportedly remained in regular contact with the ousted Nvidia co-founder.
